questions.q: Acetaldehyde is treated with a catalytic amount of aluminium ethoxide, Al(OC₂H₅)₃, under anhydrous conditions. The main product is:
questions.explain: In the Tishchenko reaction two aldehyde molecules combine into one ester: CH₃CO– from the aldehyde that lost a hydride and –OCH₂CH₃ from the one that gained it. The aldol product is the trap, because Al(OEt)₃ does not cause aldol reaction even though acetaldehyde has α-hydrogens.

questions.q: Which statement is true for the Tishchenko reaction but NOT for the Cannizzaro reaction?
options: It involves transfer of a hydride ion
It is a disproportionation of an aldehyde
It works for aldehydes that have α-hydrogens
It requires concentrated NaOH or KOH
questions.explain: Both reactions are aldehyde disproportionations by hydride transfer, but Cannizzaro needs an aldehyde without α-H, whereas the aluminium alkoxide in Tishchenko works with or without α-H. Concentrated hydroxide is the Cannizzaro reagent, not the Tishchenko one.

questions.q: Aluminium isopropoxide, Al(OCH(CH₃)₂)₃, in isopropanol converts a ketone into a secondary alcohol. This reaction is the:
questions.explain: Al(OCH(CH₃)₂)₃ with isopropanol reduces C=O to CH–OH, the MPV reduction. Oppenauer oxidation goes the other way (alcohol to carbonyl, with excess acetone), and Tishchenko uses Al(OC₂H₅)₃ with the aldehyde alone.

questions.q: The aldehyde shown is treated with Al(OC₂H₅)₃. Which ester is formed?
questions.explain: Both halves of a Tishchenko ester keep the skeleton of the starting aldehyde: the acid part is C₆H₅CH₂COO– and the alcohol part is –OCH₂CH₂C₆H₅. Benzyl benzoate is what benzaldehyde gives, not phenylacetaldehyde.
